messages:
Maria (CS): FYI — AcroData hit a production regression: embeddings calls are returning 403 with 'missing scope: embeddings.create'. Started yesterday evening after a service key rotation. Customer traffic impacted (search relevance).

Samir (ENG): can you paste the raw error and a quick repro? also which key did they rotate (SSO or service account)? @Alex R. in case infra mapping matters.

Maria (CS): repro (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"text-embed-large","input":"hello"}'
```
response:
```json
{"error":{"message":"missing scope: embeddings.create","code":403}}
```
They say the rotation was done via our SSO portal (service account key).

Samir (ENG): thank you. that error text is definitive. my guess: the provisioner that issues service keys skipped the embeddings scope. Can you share the provisioner YAML or the SSO audit log entry?

Maria (CS): copied from audit (redacted):
```yaml
service_key:
  name: acrodata-svc
  scopes:
    - rerank
    - model:read
```
(no embeddings, no inference.generate)

Alex R.: ugh — I remember we had a templating change in the provisioner CR that accidentally filtered scopes when a feature flag was off. @provisioner-bot did we run a rollout last week?

provisioner-bot: rolled out provisioner v1.2.3 to prod on 2025-11-04T03:12:14Z (canary 3/5) — config-templates updated.

Jesse (SRE): looking at recent deploys + audits: there is a delta where the new template uses a map for scopes and our merge script only handles lists. result: embeddings scope omitted for service keys created during that window.

Samir (ENG): ok action plan: 1) generate a short-term remediation (patch existing service keys for affected customers), 2) fix provisioner template code and roll out, 3) rotate keys for security hygiene, 4) follow up with customer and open incident postmortem.

Maria (CS): customer asked for ETA — they need a patch within 2 hours or they'll failover. can we do hotfix?

Samir (ENG): yes. I can run a quick patch script that adds the missing scopes to the service_key entry in SSO and re-issue the key without a full rotate (if the platform supports add-only). If not, we'll rotate. Sample patch (what I'll run):
```bash
# add scope to existing service key record
curl -X PATCH https://sso.redwood.ai/api/service-keys/acrodata-svc \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scopes":["rerank","model:read","embeddings.create","inference.generate"]}'
```
This will keep the UUID but update scopes. If that hits issues, fallback is rotate.

Alex R.: I can prep the provisioner patch. root cause: our template merge uses `scopes = concat(base.scopes, override.scopes)` but the override was a map so concat returned nil. I'll change to defensive logic and add a unit test.

provisioner-bot: created PR #412: fix/scope-merge-for-service-keys — tests added.

deploy-bot: starting canary deploy of provisioner v1.2.4 to staging -> production (canary: 2/5). rolling back if errors > 0.5%

Jesse (SRE): beware: updating service keys in place won't invalidate tokens. if customer already has a token issued missing the scope, they'll still get 403 until they fetch a new key/token. recommend instructing customer to rotate on their side OR we can issue a rekey endpoint that returns a new token.

Samir (ENG): good point. will include rotate option. Rotation command for customer (portal):
```bash
curl -X POST https://sso.redwood.ai/api/keys/rotate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{"service_key":"acrodata-svc"}'
```
This returns a new `client_secret` they can swap in app config.

Maria (CS): I sent instructions to AcroData: 1) run the rotate endpoint or click 'Reissue key' in SSO console, 2) verify embeddings calls succeed, 3) let us know if any other routes affected.

(10m later) Maria (CS): AcroData confirms they rotated and reported success: embeddings calls now succeed (no 403). they also asked for a postmortem and mitigation so they can communicate internally.

Samir (ENG): reopening the provisioning test suite and adding integration test to block regressions (ensure list/map handling for scopes). I'll also schedule a backfill to patch any other affected service keys created between 2025-11-04T03:00Z and 2025-11-04T06:00Z.

Alex R.: leaving a note to product: maybe we should expose scope-checker in SSO UI so customers see what scopes a key has before rotation (prevents surprises).

Maria (CS): thanks team — customer happy for now. I'll file the incident and attach this thread + timelines for the postmortem. :thumbsup:

Jesse (SRE): closing loop: provisioner v1.2.4 deployed to prod (no rollback), backfill patch scheduled, impacted customer remediated.

Samir (ENG): will follow up with a short write-up and the exact list of patched service keys for compliance.

Maria (CS): adding to ticket #INC-2025-442.
